fixes.explanation: The text says otherwise, friend. Luke writes, “Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God.” They were filled with awe, and they said, “We have seen remarkable things today.” That doesn't sound unsure to me.
Yes, baker. Luke writes, “Everyone was taken with amazement and glorified God.” They were filled with awe, and they said, “We have seen remarkable things today.” That's not a crowd leaving unsure.

Look again at his words, friend. He says, “Lord, if You are willing, You can make me clean.” He says “You can,” and the “if” sits on whether Jesus is willing. Jesus answers that “if” right away: “I am willing…” (Luke 5:13)
Right, baker. The man says, “…You can make me clean.” His words say Jesus can, and the “if” is about whether Jesus is willing. Then Jesus tells him, “I am willing…” (Luke 5:13)
By sundown isn't what the text says, friend. Luke says, “And immediately the leprosy left him.” Jesus says, “Be clean!” and the leprosy leaves right then. Nobody has to keep an eye on the sky.

Within seven days sounds close, baker, but Luke gives a tighter time. He says, “And immediately the leprosy left him.” Jesus speaks, and that's the moment it goes. Seven days is how long my dough sits when I forget about it.

Yes, baker. Jesus says, “…go, show yourself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for your cleansing, as a testimony to them.” The priest is the one Jesus names. The man gets clear directions.

No king in this verse, friend. Jesus tells the man to show himself to the priest. The offering is the one Moses prescribed for his cleansing. I'd have to imagine a whole palace trip, and the text doesn't give one.

Elders are a fair guess, baker, but they aren't who Jesus names. He says to show himself to the priest and present the offering Moses prescribed for his cleansing. The one name for who the man shows himself to is the priest.

Yes, baker. Luke says, “…they could not find a way through the crowd.” The place is packed, and they can't find a way in. I get it. I once tried to reach the last cookie at a full counter and gave up.
No door trouble is mentioned, friend. Luke says, “…they could not find a way through the crowd.” The crowd is what stops them. Nobody mentions a lock at all.
That's it, baker. Luke says, “When Jesus saw their faith, He said…” The men carried the paralyzed man and lowered him through the tiles. Jesus sees their faith. The word is faith.
Yes, baker. Jesus says to him, “Friend, your sins are forgiven.” That's the first thing He says to the paralyzed man. It isn't a command to walk. It's forgiveness first.

Moses is a big name, baker, but he's not who the scribes and Pharisees name in their thoughts. They think, “Who can forgive sins but God alone?” God alone is the phrase. Moses doesn't come up in their thinking.
That's it, baker. Jesus says, “…get up, pick up your mat, and go home.” Three things in one sentence, and the mat is the middle one. A man who's been lying on a mat gets a to-do list.

Some men carried him in, baker, so that's a fair guess. But Jesus says, “…get up, pick up your mat, and go home.” Luke says the man “…took what he had been lying on…” The text doesn't have him handing it off.
The men who brought him did a lot, friend. They lowered him through the tiles. But the text says he “…went home glorifying God.” That's what Luke tells us he's doing on the way.
